newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property stocks in demand, more rises expected.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks in demand, more rises expected.

text.p: Property stocks rebounded on Monday, buoyed by bargain-hunting and optimism over the sector's fundamentals after recent weakness, analysts said.
The HSI-Properties sub-index closed up 938.95 points or 3.95 percent, at 24,719.43, well ahead of the Hang Seng Index which rose 317.64 points, or 2.43 percent, to 13,399.34.
"This little lull we've been going through doesn't mean a thing," said Salomon Brothers analyst Michael Green, who recently issued a bullish report on the sector.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd, which last month said it would launch five or six residential projects worth HK$20 billion (US$2.58 billion) in 1997, leapt HK$3.00 to HK$70.50.

Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, which has said it and a unit of Swire Pacific Ltd had won the right to redevelop a site in Hong Kong with an estimated cost of more than HK$25 billion, rose HK$3.00 to HK$90.50.
Swire rose HK$1.75 to HK$61.50 and New World Development Co Ltd gained HK$2.80 to HK$48.50.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$2.75 to HK$73.50.
Green expects further gains, and said a recent correction in property shares was excessive.
The sector has been under selling pressure in recent weeks after the government announced plans to clip speculators' wings.
It ordered developers to sell at least 20 percent of each development in the initial launch, and to presell the entire development within six months of winning presale consent.
But while the changes might have cooled buying pressure, they had not sent the sector into a decline, analysts said.
"My view is that the (underlying) cycle is upward. And it's just trying to get a bit of a breather before the handover," said Colliers Jardine analyst Spencer Davies.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
"The market way over-discounted what was happening," said an analyst with a U.S. investment bank, who declined to be named.
There was evidence of the sector's robustness late on Monday when the government released data showing sale and purchase agreements for all types of building units rocketed in April.
Despite the bid to cool the market, sale and purchase agreements rose 58.6 percent compared to March, and 166.2 percent compared to April 1996.
While the government planned to boost next year's housing supply figure to 35,000 residential units, this was still close to the average annual supply in the 1980s and early 1990s, analysts said.
Tim Kirkus, associate director with property agent Richard Ellis, which specialises in the luxury end of the market, said his company had experienced a busy first three months of 1997.
Kirkus said prices of luxury units on Hong Kong island increased by about 18 percent year-on-year in the first quarter.
"Yes, there's a reduction in speculative investment, but the deals are being done," Kirkus said.
Interest fears -- cited as a factor in recent declines among property stocks -- were not a concern for speculators, he said.
"If you're going to speculate, you're going to speculate anyway in that sort of sector," Kirkus said.
